text: GENERALIZATION CORRECTION (round-69, user: CodeTerm is a shipped orchestration product — the standard must work for ANY project with branching, not for developing codeterm itself). SUPERSEDES the doc-home in the body: the canonical home of the lifecycle standard is an EMBEDDED PRODUCT DOC — new tier-3 doc served as 'codeterm docs LANES' (include_str like ORCHESTRATION.md, add to the docs registry + the orphan-loader test from task_52539b4e), NOT docs/contributing/lanes.md. The worker_suffix pointer line becomes 'Lane lifecycle: codeterm docs LANES' — resolvable in EVERY project the product runs in. docs/contributing/lanes.md in this repo becomes a thin pointer for human contributors (one paragraph + 'run codeterm docs LANES'). CONTENT RULE for the embedded doc: zero references to this repo's specifics — no feat/canvas-updates, no build.sh, no scripts/test-capped.sh; the standard speaks in product concepts only (integration head, task short-id, plan qa, worktrees). Verify every other task in this process wave for the same leak: spawn guard, naming check, code-only detection, auto-cleanup are all product code (already general); the ONLY repo-local artifact allowed is the thin contributor pointer.

PROCESS-WAVE CHARTER (round-71, binding for ALL process-wave lanes: 5a6d58c5, 46d7cc4c, 4fc2ae89, 540e7afa, 310d7e6b, d1450940, 3165f160, 7140a28c, 1d0572d0 — each gate checks conformance to this stride). THREE CORRECTIONS: (1) ONE-QA-GATE-PER-MACHINE is a GLOBAL PRODUCT INVARIANT, not a this-plan convention. Rationale goes into the embedded doc verbatim-in-spirit: multiple worktrees building on one machine cause cache churn, rebuild races, lock contention, and duplicate platform verification — therefore heavy gates (builds, clippy, suites, e2e) run in EXACTLY ONE registered QA lane per machine, owned by the orchestrator; simple workers are STRUCTURALLY UNABLE to run them (registry-keyed detection + report template that only REQUESTS gates), not merely forbidden by prose. Workers request via GATES REQUESTED; the orchestrator's queue executes. (2) NO REPO-SPECIFIC ASSUMPTIONS anywhere in the wave: no per-worker gates, no machine names, no repo paths/branch names in product code or embedded docs — the works-in-a-stranger's-repo check applies to every lane's gate. (3) INTEGRATION CHECKOUT BRANCH RULE (user correction, verbatim intent): the integration checkout stays on the ACTUAL target branch being integrated (e.g. the feature or develop branch itself) — never an ad-hoc 'integrate-*' staging branch UNLESS explicitly staging with a recorded reason. Lifecycle point 2 of the embedded doc updates accordingly: lanes fork from the integration head = the target branch's head; the spawn guard's canonical-checkout predicate is unaffected (it keys on checkout identity, not branch name), but plan lanes and auto-cleanup treat 'integration head' as the target branch tip.

SCOPE ADDITION — DELIVERABLE 5 (round-74, Orchestrator incident: 'git push origin --delete <branch>' fired the pre-push FULL hook and launched cargo check during cleanup — interrupted by hand). PRINCIPLE for the standard doc: CLEANUP OPERATIONS ARE GATE-FREE — deleting a branch/worktree verifies nothing new; heavy gates guard content INTEGRATION, not content REMOVAL. MECHANICAL FIX (this repo's .githooks/pre-push, ~5 lines): the hook reads ref updates from stdin — when EVERY pushed ref is a deletion (local sha is the zero-sha), exit 0 before any check; mixed pushes (deletion + real ref) still gate the real refs. Do NOT document --no-verify as the cleanup path — training agents to bypass hooks resurrects the class this whole wave kills; the hook must simply be correct about what a deletion is. INHERITANCE: the auto-cleanup lane (task_540e7afa) performs programmatic branch deletions — its acceptance gains a drill: branch delete via the daemon triggers zero gate processes (ps-scan proof during the drill). Lifecycle doc line: 'Deleting branches and removing worktrees never runs gates; if a deletion asks you to compile something, the hook is wrong — fix the hook, do not bypass it.'

CHARTER ADDITION (round-77, Andrey verbatim intent: 'Бери пики под запрет тотальный'): CHERRY-PICKS ARE BANNED, totally. Lifecycle doc gains the rule: lane content moves ONLY by merge (or rebase of an unmerged lane onto the target head) — never cherry-pick; cherry-picking duplicates commits with new shas, breaking merged-vs-unmerged tracking ('иначе мы не знаем что смерджено что нет'), ancestry-based cleanup (auto-cleanup's merged check), and plan lanes verdicts. Worktrees must merge normally; branching stays simple: lane forks from target head, merges back whole. Exception path: none in the standard; salvaging partial work = new lane from head + manual porting, recorded as a stride. Enforcement stitch (small): the report refusal warns when HEAD's ancestry does not include the recorded lane branch point (cherry-picked/duplicated content smell) — warn-tier, not refuse (detection is heuristic).

LOAD INCIDENT ADDENDUM (round-84, live: Mac-Air crawling under 5 editing agents): two stacked causes confirmed — (1) prod CodeTerm 1.6.2 runs WITHOUT every perf fix shipped on the branch (chat virtualization #189, memoized surfaces, longtask fixes): daemon 140% CPU + WebContent 1.3GB/130% under 5 streaming agents is exactly the fixed bug class, cure = the release itself; (2) the pre-push FULL gate fired a whole-crate cargo check locally (rustc 1.1GB RSS) because integration-branch pushes run the full gate BY DESIGN — on a weak machine during endgame this stacks onto agent load. Lifecycle-doc line to add: on constrained machines, integration pushes use PREPUSH_LIGHT=1 with heavy verification routed through the QA/builder gate (which the endgame flow does anyway), or push integration merges from a builder machine.

FIX-WHERE-THE-GATE-LIVES RULE (round-87, Andrey via Orchestrator — clarifying addition to the lifecycle standard, also recorded against the QA task's registry design): for tight RED->small-fix->rerun loops, when a remote machine owns the relevant warm worktree/gate AND the fix is local to that gate's findings, spawn a REAL CodeTerm worker ON that machine (workspace + agent spawn --mesh, bound to the task, lane branch fetched there) to fix and rerun that machine's single QA gate in place — instead of ping-ponging text through the orchestrator and a local worker (each round-trip costs a full report/redispatch cycle for a one-line fix). ALL INVARIANTS PRESERVED, explicitly: one heavy gate per physical machine (the remote worker uses THAT machine's registered gate, nothing new); real worker panes only, never ad-hoc chat; branch/task binding visible (lane fields set at spawn); orchestrator retains merge/accept authority — the remote worker reports in_review like any lane, it just iterates against the gate locally. DECISION HEURISTIC for the doc: fix-loop lives WHERE THE REPRO LIVES — local repro -> local worker; remote-only repro/gate -> remote worker; cross-machine fixes (code here, verify there) -> local worker + remote gate routing as before.

QA-FIXER MODE (round-88, Andrey via Orchestrator — companion to 'fix-loop lives where the repro lives'): a QA lane that has ALREADY ISOLATED the cause may switch modes from reporter to fixer when the fix is local to its own failing gate — amend the lane branch, push, rerun its OWN gate, report the final verdict — instead of bouncing a diagnosed one-liner back through the orchestrator. This is a MODE SWITCH on the same machine, not a new lane: the QA pane operates as a real CodeTerm worker with visible lane/task binding (never ad-hoc chat). CONSTRAINTS, unchanged and explicit: one heavy gate per physical machine (QA-fixer reruns the gate it already owns — nothing new spawns); no cherry-picks (amend/commit on the lane branch, merge-only flow); branch/task binding visible (its fixes are lane commits, attributable); orchestrator retains final accept/merge — QA-fixer's green is evidence, not acceptance. SCOPE BOUNDARY (keeps the mode honest): QA may fix what its gate DIAGNOSED (fixture drift, missing manifest regeneration, fmt, a test asserting stale copy, an isolated one-line defect its trace pinpoints); anything requiring design judgment or touching code beyond the diagnosed failure goes back through the normal bounce — QA-fixer is a shortcut for MECHANICAL closure of an isolated diagnosis, not a second implementation lane. The lifecycle doc gets both rules as one subsection: 'Where fixes happen: the fix-loop lives where the repro lives; a QA gate that isolated the cause may close it in place.'
